![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14221452/assets/3bde5b93aa28654977fdb55b0b2808fde2fb2f54ba33a6e9a2a4281b6966682f.png)

Which of the following gives the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x={t}^{4}-2{t}^{2},\,y={t}^{3}-1
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [1,\sqrt{2}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-2{t}^{2}) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-4t \\  & =4t({t}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}({t}^{3}-1)4t({t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}t({t}^{3}-1)({t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a positive number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\ge 0$ for all $t\in [1,\sqrt{2}].$

Therefore, the area is given by

$$
A=4{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}t({t}^{3}-1)({t}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}t.
$$
